entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) is a prominent Czech political entity founded on April 21, 1991, in Prague, emerging from the political transformations that followed the Velvet Revolution of 1989. It has played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of the Czech Republic, advocating for liberal-conservative policies, economic reform, and European integration. Notable figures include Václav Klaus, the party's first leader and a former Czech president, who has been instrumental in its ideological development and political strategies.

In the years following its establishment, the ODS became a dominant force in Czech politics, securing victories in parliamentary elections, particularly in 1996 when it won 27.7% of the vote, leading to Klaus becoming Prime Minister. The party's policies have often emphasized free-market economics, privatization, and reducing the role of the state in the economy, contributing to significant economic transformations in post-communist Czech society. The ODS has also been involved in various coalition governments, impacting legislative frameworks and national policies.

The legacy of the Civic Democratic Party is evident in its influence on the direction of Czech politics, particularly in promoting a center-right agenda that has shaped public discourse on economic and social issues. Its impact can be felt in the ongoing debates about national identity, European integration, and economic policy in the Czech Republic. As of 2023, the party continues to play a key role in the political arena, facing challenges from emerging political movements and shifting public sentiments.
